acceptance_criteria.criterion: With valid config: prints confirmation message with resolved paths.
With missing config: prints missing-config error to stderr, exits with code 1.
With invalid config: prints validation error to stderr, exits with code 1.
No unhandled exceptions — top-level error handling in place.

summary: Replaced the placeholder in src/index.ts with a shebang-equipped binary entry point.
Calls loadConfig() inside a top-level try/catch; on success prints resolved config values to stdout; on any error writes to process.stderr and exits with code 1.
TypeScript build clean; all 9 acceptance-criteria checks pass (AC1–AC5 + edge cases).

comments.note: src/index.ts currently logs all five config fields at startup; once additional commands/sub-systems are wired up, consider moving the verbose config dump to a --verbose flag to avoid cluttering normal output.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified through live execution of dist/index.js.
Build clean (npm run build, tsc, no errors).
AC1: shebang confirmed on line 1 of both src/index.ts and dist/index.js.
AC2: valid config prints confirmation message with all 5 resolved field values to stdout, exits 0.
AC3: missing config.json prints human-readable error to stderr, exits 1; stdout is empty.
AC4: config with missing required field and config with empty-string required field both print validation error to stderr, exit 1.
AC5: no unhandled exceptions — malformed JSON and directory-as-config edge cases are both caught and exit cleanly with code 1.
Stderr/stdout separation verified by piping each stream independently.

comments.note: Error messages correctly reference the config.json path, making them actionable for end users. No issues found.

Edge case: malformed JSON produces a parser error message (not a 'File not found' path) which surfaces the raw JSON parse error string — adequate for a developer tool, but consider a friendlier message in a future iteration.

summary: src/index.ts is a clean, minimal binary entry point. All 5 acceptance criteria met and verified by QA.
No Blocking issues. No Fix-Forward edits applied — code already follows best practices and requires no non-behavioral corrections.
Stream separation is correct: console.log routes success output to stdout; process.stderr.write routes error output to stderr; process.exit(1) is used on failure.
The (err as Error) type cast is safe in context — loadConfig() exclusively throws new Error(...) instances.
The verbose config dump (all 5 fields at startup) is acknowledged low-priority technical debt, already flagged by the Developer. Suitable for a --verbose flag once subcommands are wired up.
Tagged one documentation-forward for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: The verbose 5-field config dump at startup is acknowledged technical debt. Once subcommands exist, this output should be gated behind a --verbose flag to avoid cluttering normal invocations.

[documentation-forward] src/index.ts has no module-level comment. A brief JSDoc block or inline comment explaining that this is the CLI entry point, what it does on success vs. failure, and how to prepare config.json would benefit future contributors.

No issues — code is clean and consistent. The (err as Error) cast in the catch block is safe given loadConfig() always throws Error instances, and could be made more defensive with an instanceof guard in a future pass if error sources broaden.
